root_cause: The _keydown handler in tab.js uses getNextActiveElement without checking whether the target tab is disabled, allowing focus to move to a disabled tab when arrow keys are pressed.
repair_strategy: Modify the _keydown method to skip over disabled tabs by repeatedly calling getNextActiveElement in the navigation direction until an enabled tab is found or a safe iteration limit is reached.
expected_accessibility_effect: ArrowRight will now move focus to the next enabled tab (Billing) skipping the disabled Notifications tab, updating aria-selected and focus accordingly, and ArrowLeft will wrap to the last enabled tab.
functional_risks: Infinite loop mitigated by length check; if all tabs are disabled, the last checked disabled tab may be selected.
Behavior change if tabs are disabled after initialization; the navigation will skip them as intended.
Ensure that show() is not called on a disabled tab; the loop prevents this unless all tabs are disabled.
verification_requirements: Press ArrowRight from Account tab → Billing tab becomes aria-selected=true and receives focus.
Press ArrowLeft from Billing tab → Account tab becomes aria-selected=true and receives focus (wrapping if needed).
Repeated ArrowRight/Left navigation skips the disabled Notifications tab.
Screen reader announces the newly selected tab.
Tab panel visibility updates correctly when tab changes.
